Definition: of Latin origin; apparently swinish; Porcius, a Roman:--Porcius.
BiblicalUsage: Porcius Festus is the Roman governor who succeeded Felix, and Luke names him once. He came into Felix's room, and Paul's case passed into his hands, carrying the apostle one step closer to Rome.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God moves his servants through the hands of governors who never know they are part of his plan.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
